assessment_notes: growth-in-arena breaks the never-move guarantee for in-block koshes: a new slot means a new address; an alias taken before growth reads the abandoned slot (stale, not crashed — the slot stays mapped until block exit); outside-block koshes keep their region and guarantee; no example aliases a growing in-block kosh today, so nothing breaks, but the guarantee becomes 'where you make it' in a second sense

parimita fits the design (growth waste counts against the arena budget, so waste cannot run away; budget and block become one mechanism); what bounds an UNBUDGETED block's arena is not stated — that size is the design's to name
the design must answer whether the post-block-use check stays: 287's golden is a clean E_KOSH_MANDAPA stop; without the check it becomes a crash (unmapped arena) or a garbage read (reused arena)

no function returns a whole kosh (checked: nivartanam returns values, elements, and lengths, never a kosh itself), so the dynamic question (a kosh created by a call inside a block) does not arise in the tree; the textual count is complete
ws1_arena_breakage.count_method: a kosh counts as made inside a mandapa if its declaration is textually inside a mandapa block — braced (mandapa { ... }) or indented (mandapa + indented body), including the typed form (kosh dasham m[2], 299's form, which a naive 'kosh NAME[' pattern misses); it counts as used after if its name — OR any alias assigned its address inside the block (bahar = k) — is used after that block's end; a name-only count misses the alias case, and the alias case is the whole story here

examples_used_after.note: via alias: bahar = k inside the block, likha(padh(bahar, 0)) after; today it compiles, prints 22 (the in-block read), then stops with E_KOSH_MANDAPA at runtime (exit 1) — the runtime check, not a compile refusal; its golden is that stop, on v287 and v288 identically; under the arena design its fate depends on whether the check stays (unchanged) or goes (clean stop becomes crash or garbage read)

ws1_arena_breakage.verdict: cheap: zero running programs break; one error example needs the check kept; the design changes nothing that exists, provided the post-block-use check stays

ws2_kosh_cost.cap: the compiler refuses above ~256 statements in one function (khand kathan seema atikram: 256 koshes compile, 280 refuse; 1,000 plain vitti declarations with zero koshes refuse too, so the cap is general, not kosh-specific); top-level kosh declarations are a syntax error (vyakaran dosh, line 1), so koshes cannot be spread across the file to dodge the per-function cap; 1,000 simultaneously-live koshes would require global-address smuggling, not a normal program
ws2_kosh_cost.conclusion: virtual is harmless because it is virtual (MAP_NORESERVE, untouched pages cost nothing; 100 koshes reserve 6.4 GiB of address space and use 0.4 MB of RAM; 6.4 GiB is 0.005% of the 128 TiB user address space); resident cost is one 4 KiB page per kosh (the region's header page, touched at creation); touched and declared-only differ by almost nothing for small koshes (one pushed element fits in the header page)
ws2_kosh_cost.extrapolated_1000: 64 GiB virtual and ~4 MB resident, extrapolated from the measured per-kosh rates (exactly N x 64 MiB virtual, ~4 KiB RSS each) — extrapolation, not measurement; the compiler cap is the binding constraint, not memory
ws2_kosh_cost.method: probe programs declaring N live koshes, then blocking on grahan() input while /proc/<pid>/status is read (VmPeak, VmSize, VmHWM, VmRSS); two variants: declared-only (reserved, untouched) and touched (one kosh_push each)
